title: Continuous tokens/sec sentinel for PRs using rolling-reference and Bayesian drift alarms
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Add a lightweight continuous inference throughput sentinel that runs on PRs and in scheduled CI to catch regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latency before merge. This initiative focuses on a low-cost, high-signal microbenchmark that complements the heavier nightly end-to-end regressions.

Design summary:
- Microbenchmark harness: small deterministic load runner (3 warmup iterations + 30 measured iterations) that replays synthetic request traces representative of three customer-shaped scenarios (chat-short, chat-medium, long-compute). Runs on GitHub Actions runners with ephemeral CPU/GPU labels, using the same container used by the runtime integration tests.
- Metric computation: collect tokens/sec (aggregate), p50/p95/p99 latency, and sequence-length distribution. Compute a rolling-reference window composed of the last 30 successful master CI runs; use EWMA weighting (alpha=0.15) to bias recent runs while preserving long-term signal.
- Drift detection: apply a Bayesian change-point detection on the tokens/sec time series and a trimmed-mean percentile comparison for p95 to reduce sensitivity to single-run noise. A regression is flagged when: posterior probability of shift > 0.995 AND relative tokens/sec drop > 6% OR p95 increase > 12%.
- PR gating rules: the sentinel posts a GitHub check summary. Block merge only when the flagged regression is reproduced by 2 independent runs (auto-retry up to 3 runs). If block triggers, auto-run the expanded harness on a dedicated perf runner (20 iterations) and notify #perf-alerts with links to the failing traces.
- False-positive controls: environment tagging (runner type, container image sha, model weights), minimum sample thresholds, and a short calibration phase that excludes runs with excessive background noise. Allow an opt-out label (perf-ignore) for infra-only changes.

Trade-offs considered:
- Cost vs coverage: microbenchmarks chosen to keep per-PR CI time under ~6 minutes while still exercising realistic KV cache behavior; nightly end-to-end suites remain the ground truth for hard regressions.
- Sensitivity tuning: strict thresholds reduce missed regressions but increase noise; we bias toward preventing quiet regressions on model-serving kernels by requiring reproducibility across runs before gating.

Integration points & artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Throughput+Sentinel+Design
- Benchmark traces stored in BenchStore: https://benchstore.redwood.com/series/ENG-35021-sentinel (read-only links in checks)
- GitHub Actions workflow (draft): .github/workflows/perf-sentinel.yml (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4891)
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/PerfSentinel/ci-sentinel-overview

Acceptance criteria:
- Detect synthetic tokens/sec regressions >=7% with reproducibility requirement and <=2% false-positive rate on historical replay of last 6 months of PRs.
- PR check latency (inc. auto-retries) under 20 minutes for standard CI runners, under 60 minutes when escalated to dedicated perf runner.
- Alerts post clear remediation steps and link to traces/PRs.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary: Enable sentinel on 10 low-traffic repos for two cycles and measure FP/FN.
2) Gradual: Expand to all runtime and serving repos after tuning.
3) Enforce: Make blocking only for P0/P1 tagged changes for first month, then consider expanding to all PRs if stability is high.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add sequence-length normalized metrics to avoid penalizing work that legitimately increases token output.
- Add dedicated GPU micro-runner pool for more stable measurements.
- Explore multivariate drift detection combining tokens/sec, p95 and memory footprint to reduce mode-specific false positives.
